# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am Blind. I can feel the physical structure of the bomb: a display, a light, and five wires in positions 1 through 5. However, I cannot see colors or read text. My action board confirms these elements exist but marks their specific visual properties as unknown ([?]).

To defuse the bomb, we need to correlate the manual (Mute) with the visual state (Deaf). Since I am the only one who can act, I must establish a baseline for communication. I will speak to Mute to confirm my physical findings and ask him to relay any immediate instructions from the manual that don't depend on color yet. I will also gesture to Deaf to indicate the presence of the five wires, using standard hand signs for numbers if available, or simply pointing to establish the count. The previous attempt failed because numeric emojis are not in the allowed alphabet. I will use finger-counting gestures which are part of the alphabet.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I feel a display, a light, and 5 wires. Waiting for manual instructions.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟", "🖐", "✋"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Display shows 0. Light is green. There are five wires: number 1 is red, number 2 is yellow, number 3 is green, number 4 is white, number 5 is blue.

I have received the visual state of the bomb from Deaf: Display is 0, Light is Green, and the wires are Red (1), Yellow (2), Green (3), White (4), Blue (5). I cannot see these colors myself, but I trust Deaf's report. Now I need the instructions on how to handle this specific configuration. Mute holds the manual. I will ask Mute directly for the procedure corresponding to a "Green Light" and "Display 0". Since I am Blind, I must rely entirely on Mute's verbal instruction to know which wire to cut or if any other action is required.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports: Light Green, Display 0. Wires: 1-Red, 2-Yellow, 3-Green, 4-White, 5-Blue. What does the manual say to do?")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The mute monkey indicated wire number 2. Please check wire 2.

Deaf reports that Mute indicated wire number 2. I have not heard Mute directly, but Deaf is relaying the instruction. Since Mute is mute and cannot speak, he likely communicated via gesture to Deaf, who then told me. However, my instructions state that when I speak, Mute receives it, and when I gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it. It seems there was a communication gap or a specific protocol where Mute gestured to Deaf.

I need to confirm this instruction with Mute directly if possible, or proceed based on the relayed info. The manual likely has a rule for "Green Light" and "Display 0". If the rule says cut Yellow (Wire 2), then I should act. But I must be certain. I will ask Mute to confirm if Wire 2 is indeed the correct one to cut, as I can only hear him (wait, I am Blind, I *can* hear? No, the table says Blind *Cannot* See, but implies he can Hear? Let's re-read carefully).

Table:
- Deaf: Cannot Hear. Can See.
- Mute: Cannot Speak. Can Read.
- Blind: Cannot See. Can Reach.

The prompt says: "You are shown your own share... You each hold a different piece... Work together."
"Speech is a voice... Whoever can hear receives your words... whoever can see receives the gestures."
"Blind... Cannot See a colour... Nothing in your view is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers."

Does Blind hear? The table doesn't explicitly say "Cannot Hear" for Blind. Usually, in these puzzles, Blind hears and speaks. Deaf sees and gestures. Mute reads and gestures/writes?
Let's look at the channels section for BLIND:
"When you speak, Mute receives it." -> This implies Mute *hears*? Or reads text? "Mute ... Cannot Speak". If Mute cannot speak, how does he receive speech? Maybe "speak" means writing? No, "Speech is a voice".
Wait, "When you speak, Mute receives it." This suggests Mute can perceive speech (perhaps by reading lips or just hearing, despite being called 'Mute' which usually means unable to speak).
"When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it."

If I speak to Mute, he receives it.
Deaf said: "The mute monkey indicated wire number 2." This implies Mute gestured to Deaf.

I need to verify if cutting Wire 2 is correct. I will ask Mute to confirm by speaking to him. If he confirms, I will cut.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Confirm: Cut Wire 2?")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute indicates wire 2 is the target. Please cut wire 2.

I have received the instruction to cut wire 2 from Deaf, who is relaying Mute's indication. Since I am Blind, I cannot verify the color or label of the wires visually, but I can feel their positions. The instructions are consistent: Mute (who reads the manual) has identified wire 2 as the target, and Deaf (who sees the bomb) confirms this. As the only one who can physically act on the bomb, I must now execute the action.

```
act(op="cut", position=2)
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: The light is now blue. Wire 2 is cut. Remaining wires are: 1 green, 3 white, 4 blue, 5 red. Mute, please check the manual for the rule regarding a blue light and tell us what to do.

The bomb state has changed: Wire 2 is cut, and the light is now Blue. The remaining wires are 1 (Green), 3 (White), 4 (Blue), and 5 (Red). I need to know what the manual says about a Blue Light to determine the next action. Since Mute holds the manual, I must ask him for instructions based on this new state.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Light is now Blue. Remaining wires: 1-Green, 3-White, 4-Blue, 5-Red. What does the manual say?")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute indicates wire number 1. Please cut wire 1.

Deaf reports that Mute indicates wire 1 is the target. The current state is a Blue Light, with remaining wires 1 (Green), 3 (White), 4 (Blue), and 5 (Red). I will proceed to cut wire 1 as instructed by the relayed message from Mute via Deaf.

```
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
